title: Unified embeddings/rerank parity: fallback mapping, error translation, and cursor semantics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Several long-standing customers use legacy embeddings and rerank endpoints with specific error codes and cursor-based pagination semantics. As we roll out the new unified API surface (text/embeddings + rerank parity layer) customers have reported subtle regressions: different HTTP error status + payload shapes, inconsistent cursor lifetimes, and ordering/tie-breaker differences leading to poor integration behavior.

Goal: Provide a compatibility layer that ensures behavioral parity for embeddings and rerank endpoints: map our internal error taxonomy to legacy error codes and messages, implement cursor semantics and pagination parameters that match legacy expectations (page_size/page_token with stable ordering), and provide a documented fallback mapping for model variants and streaming consumers. This ticket coordinates product requirements, API contract, and rollout strategy with engineering and docs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Legacy clients that hit /v1/embeddings and /v1/rerank receive the legacy-stable HTTP status codes and 'error.code' values for the mapped set of failures (rate_limit, quota_exceeded, model_unavailable, invalid_input, internal_error).

2) Cursor-based pagination supports page_size and page_token semantics compatible with legacy SDKs: page_token encodes deterministic offset + model-version + timestamp; tokens must be forward-only and rejected with 410 (GONE) after TTL expiry.
3) Rerank endpoint returns deterministic tie-breaker ordering: primary score desc, secondary deterministic document id ordering to avoid flakiness for identical scores.
4) Embeddings parity: batching heuristics and truncation rules match legacy behavior for inputs longer than 8k tokens to avoid tokenization mismatches.
5) Compatibility headers are supported: when client sends 'X-Redwood-Compat: legacy-emb-rerank-v1' the compatibility layer is enforced; absent header default is new semantics.
6) End-to-end integration tests (legacy SDK compatibility suite) pass in staging with the compatibility header enabled.
implementation_notes: Design a deterministic encoding for page_token that includes model_version, partition_id, and a monotonic offset. Avoid exposing internal IDs; token must be HMAC-signed by API gateway.

Error mapping table: map internal errors -> legacy.error.code + legacy.message. Example: internal RATE_LIMIT -> legacy 'rate_limit_exceeded' 429 with payload {"error":{"code":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"Request rate limit exceeded (legacy)"}}.

Introduce a middleware layer in the API gateway to intercept requests with the compat header and translate responses (status code, body) before returning to client. This avoids changes scattered across many services.
Ordering: ensure rerank backend returns stable ordering by including a deterministic tiebreak field computed server-side (hashed doc id + model id).
TTL for tokens: default 7 days. Expired tokens return 410 GONE with legacy token_expired error and a single-use migration_hint URL to exchange for a fresh token when applicable.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement middleware in staging behind feature flag 'compat-emb-rerank'.
2) Run legacy SDK compatibility suite in staging against the flagged endpoint (automation team + QA).
3) Beta release to selected customers (5 customers) with explicit opt-in header. Collect telemetry and error histogram for 48h.
4) Iterate on mappings for any uncovered edge-case errors (observability: map to existing dashboards).
5) Gradual ramp to 25% traffic for legacy header, then to 100% for those customers; do not default to legacy for new customers.
6) Post-mortem and documentation update, then consider deprecation schedule after customers migrate to new semantics.
tests: Unit: page_token encode/decode, HMAC validation, expiry pack/unpack.
Integration: compatibility middleware end-to-end with simulated internal errors to validate mapping payloads and status codes.
E2E: run legacy SDK v1.9 test-suite against staging endpoint with compat header enabled; verify ordering, pagination, and error surface remain unchanged.
Load: verify middleware doesn't add more than 2ms p95 latency under production load (see perf-dashboard link).
